messages:
maria: quick sync — we've got inconsistent cost attribution when spans don't have a stable id. can we agree on a canonical span identifier format so enrichment and billing can join reliably?

devin: +1 we need something deterministic. option A: canonical = hash(service + ':' + trace_id + ':' + span_id) (first 16 hex). option B: structured string like service:trace:span. tradeoffs: A is fixed width (low cardinality footprint), B is human readable.

sam: for rollout we need a backward-compat plan. most agents currently only set request_id header. can we make agents emit both request_id and canonical for a transitional window?

jordan: ingest pipeline constraint: cost enrichment runs in the early enrich stage before heavy joins. if canonical_id isn't present we either compute it pre-enrich (cheaper) or rely on request_id->canonical mapping later (expensive). leaning to compute canonical early.

katie: from product/analytics POV dashboards currently group by request_id. we need mapping preserved for at least 30d during cutover. also want a flag we can filter on to compare before/after.

maria: rough proposal: 1) define canonical format (devin pick one) 2) agents emit both headers (X-Span-Canonical + X-Request-Id) 3) ingest: compute canonical if header missing in pre_enrich 4) canary by service + region 5) run incremental backfill 90d 6) remove request_id-dep after 3mo observation.

devin: leaning to option A (hashed 16 hex) to avoid explosion in storage indexes. example implement:
```
// pseudo
payload = service + ':' + trace_id + ':' + span_id
canonical = sha256(payload).slice(0,16)
set_header('X-Span-Canonical', canonical)
```
This keeps keys fixed-length and friendly for our shard keys.

sam: ok. two notes — 1) hashing means we need deterministic normalization (service case, hostname aliases) before hash, 2) we must add a "canonical_source" enum to trace envelope so we know whether it was agent-provided or computed at ingest.

jordan: agree on normalization. propose small pre_enrich pipeline update:
```
ingest:
  pre_enrich:
    - normalize_service_name
    - compute_canonical_id  # use header if present else compute
  enrich:
    - attach_billing_key
    - cost_aggregation
```
This ensures cost joins use canonical id.

katie: timeline? product needs a canary window and metrics to validate parity (cost delta < 1% per service). also want a dashboard comparing group counts by request_id vs canonical.

maria: suggested timeline: RFC this week, agent PRs next 2 weeks, ingest rollout + canary 1 week, backfill job scheduled during canary, monitor 4 weeks, then wider rollout.

devin: backfill cost concern — full 90d backfill will read a lot of raw traces. prefer tenant-scoped incremental backfills and to expose backfill op in ops console. also tag backfilled rows with `canonical_backfilled=true`.

sam: for ops runbook add steps: how to revert (switch ingest back to mapping table), how to force re-compute for a service, and how to run one-off backfill. example command for infra: `python infra/tools/backfill_canonical.py --days 90 --tenant acme --concurrency 20`

maria: good. can we get a short RFC doc with the hash format, normalization rules, ingest config patch and runbook? I'll put ownership on eng-platform + devex to coordinate agent changes.

obs-bot: RFC draft uploaded: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2170012345-span-canonical-id (please review) :eyes:

devin: I'll write the canonicalization snippet + normalization rules today. assigning myself for agent changes.

katie: I'll sketch the dashboard parity checks and sample queries.

sam: I'll prepare ingest patch and runbook. can we add a metric `canonical_mapped` to the pipeline so we can chart adoption? :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all — goal: land RFC + agent PRs by next Tue, ingest canary mid-next-week. we'll reconvene after RFC comments.
